To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the presence of wind turbine generators may increase the risk of Loss- Of-Load, but it is also possible to minimize this risk, by increasing the energy reserve and reducing the risk of Loss-of-Load Probability, while reducing the emissions.

1) the inclusion of wind turbine generators in energy reserve management can reduce the cost of emissions, and 2) the inclusion of the cost of emissions in the reserve management can reduce risk of system failure, thus improving system reliability and well-being.
the presence of wind turbines in the reserve mix is a key factor for the reduction of emissions and for the achievement of a more efficient risk management.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the assessment of the energy reserve required to achieve the expected system risk of loss of load in the presence of a variable wind power generation, taking into account the cost of emissions.

the assessment of the optimal energy reserve in the context of the presence of wind power generation plants, and the related emissions reduction, with a view to minimizing the sum of the external and industrial costs of electricity production.
the assessment of the energy reserve needed for a power system in the presence of uncertainty in production of energy due to wind speed.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
, for the case of study, the presence of wind turbines does not affect the risk of Loss- Of-Load, but it reduces the total cost of emissions.
the presence of wind turbine generators in the power system is a good solution, but the system must be able to face the uncertainty of the wind speed and the risk of loss of load.
the presence of wind power generation plants in the system is not always beneficial in terms of cost reduction, as it may lead to a significant increase of the cost of reserve.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the presence of wind turbines, as a source of energy, may lead to a reduction of the reserve needed to guarantee the expected risk of Load Loss.

the inclusion of wind generation in the system reserve calculation is beneficial in terms of cost and environmental impact, but it requires an increase in the amount of reserve to be provided by the system.

the inclusion of wind turbine generators in the energy system reserve, with a proper optimization of their number and size, allows for a significant reduction of the cost of emissions, with no increase in the cost of energy, and with an improvement of the system well-being index, as measured by the risk of Loss-of-Load.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the inclusion of wind turbine generators in the system reserve can be a valid option to achieve the expected reduction of emissions, with an increase of the risk of Loss Of Load.
the use of wind power plants is a viable option in terms of reduction of emissions.

a well-being approach to energy reserve assessment can provide a more complete picture of the problem of emissions reduction, by considering the tradeoff between emissions reduction and risk of loss of load.
